text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - German Bunds were firm but frozen in a tight range in late trade, as dealers were unwilling to enter new positions ahead of the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.51, up 0.38 points from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - British gilts settled 7/32 higher on the day but underperformed Bunds as they awaited the outcome of the U.S. FOMC meeting and the Treasury market reaction. The market has discounted a quarter point rate rise, but traders said the tone of any accompanying comments would be crucial to the reaction. June long gilt futures on LIFFE were trading at 109-17/32, up 07/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures settled higher in thin activity, with 10-year bonds outperforming Bunds. Some dealers say a 25 basis point hike in U.S. interest rates was already priced into market but others say it could still react badly. The June notionnel bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.10, up 0.24 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt futures were up around 70 basis points following rumours of a U.S. consultancy's report that the Federal Reserve would not raise rates. The firm neither confirmed nor denied the report but subscribers said no such report existed. The market has been mostly expecting a tightening from the Fed today. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 125.21, up 0.71 points from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - The prices of U.S. government securities jumped as rumours circulated on trading floors that a Washington-based consulting firm had issued a report saying the Federal Reserve would not tighten monetary policy. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-12/32, up 03/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.90 percent.

JAPAN - Key 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed firmer as fears of higher interest rates, which had dampened JGBs since late last week, withered due to the central bank's accommodative credit stance. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.32, up 0.29 points from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - A couple of high-yielding currency deals provided the only primary market business as players remained sidelined ahead of the FOMC meeting. The markets have priced in a U.S. interest rate rise of 25 basis points. The forthcoming Easter holiday will keep volumes low for the rest of the week.
